subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 3 Developments In Instrumental Jazz 1910 To Present
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: Handel's 'Messiah' belongs to which genre?
questions.explain: 'Messiah' is an English oratorio, a large sacred work for soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
End the song with a fade-out
State the main hook for the first time
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: A Lied is which type of composition?
options: A German art song for voice and piano
questions.explain: The Lied is a German Romantic art song, typically for solo voice and piano.

questions.q: In jazz harmony, 'comping' refers to...?
options: Composing a fully notated arrangement in advance
Compressing the dynamic range in the mix
Counting the band in before a number
A pianist or guitarist playing improvised, syncopated chordal accompaniment behind a soloist
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised, rhythmic chordal accompaniment provided by piano or guitar behind a soloist.

questions.q: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is an example of which Baroque genre?
questions.explain: 'The Four Seasons' consists of four solo violin concertos, a leading Baroque solo-concerto example.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: In the standard jazz turnaround, a ii-V-I progression in the key of C major uses which three chords in order?
questions.explain: In C major the supertonic seventh is Dm7, the dominant seventh is G7 and the tonic is Cmaj7.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: In a 'verse-chorus' pop structure, a 'pre-chorus' serves to...?
options: Build anticipation and lead smoothly from the verse into the chorus
questions.explain: The pre-chorus builds momentum and links the verse to the chorus.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: Programme music is best defined as which?
options: Instrumental music that depicts a narrative or extra-musical idea
Music written from a printed programme of events
questions.explain: Programme music tells a story or evokes images or ideas beyond the music itself, common in the Romantic era.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To advance the plot through speech-like singing
To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: Steve Reich is a leading composer of which 20th-century style?
questions.explain: Reich is a key minimalist, known for phasing and repetitive interlocking patterns.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: Free improvisation with no fixed form
A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
In the middle of the development only
At the very opening before the orchestra plays
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
Compressing a stereo mix into mono
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: The standard Classical string quartet comprises which instruments?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet is scored for two violins, one viola and one cello.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.
